findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a dismissed P1 is followed by a more serious finding with the same title and file.
The comparison uses raw reviewer priorities. `src/forge/autoreview.py:136-139` retains a raw P1 even when a security finding receives a Harm floor, while `src/forge/score.py:83-90,140-142` treats that finding as P0. It therefore compares equal to the dismissed P1, and `src/forge/review.py:1048-1053` carries the old dismissal, so the serious finding neither blocks nor reaches the brief. A second path bypasses this check even for a raw P0: when `forge close --dismiss` triggers a new review after a branch change, `src/forge/close.py:396-403` reapplies the requested P1 dismissal to the first result with the same title and file.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - one review reports a P0 and a P1 with the same title and file, and the P1 alone is dismissed.
The ruling does not address an earlier finding that is still open: the ceiling includes every historical finding, including the undismissed P0. On a subsequent review, that P0 sets the ceiling, so a repeated P0 is not considered higher priority and receives the P1's dismissal. Close can then mark the review clean even though nobody settled the P0.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a review repeats a dismissed P1 whose lines moved and also reports a different P0 with the same title and file.
The P0 removes the settlement for the shared identity from the whole map. The later dismissal pass therefore also reopens the repeated P1, even though its cited evidence is unchanged. It blocks and reaches the builder's brief again, contrary to the requirement that a finding whose lines only moved stay settled.
findings.title: Functional: Keep a dismissed finding settled when a sibling is more serious

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a repair review finds a serious issue, or re-reports a dismissed issue after its lines move.
The new test checks the close exit code and PR text but never runs `forge work` or checks that the serious finding reaches the builder's brief. It would pass if close blocked while the brief omitted the finding. The listed test at `tests/test_dismissals_carry_forward.py:21-35` moves the original line 3 to line 4 but reuses a finding pinned to line 3; it would pass if a line-based match incorrectly reopened a finding re-reported at line 4. These are both details of the promised behavior.
findings.title: Gate: test_dismissal_never_covers_higher_priority_finding.py and test_dismissals_carry_forward.py

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - a team upgrades an existing Forge repo.
The fix's post-merge commit messages do not state what a newly initialized or adopted repo receives and what an existing repo receives on upgrade. The supplied repository review rule requires the change to say what each receives, and the coordinator specifically requested that statement in the commit.
findings.title: Gate: State what new and existing client repos receive
